items.title: Every quasi-compact Hausdorff space has a canonical minimal extremally disconnected cover, unique up to isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file topology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that every quasi-compact Hausdorff space admits a continuous surjection from a quasi-compact Hausdorff extremally disconnected space which is minimal in the sense that no proper closed subset maps onto the target, and that such a cover is unique up to isomorphism (author lemma at source lines 5613-5624, label lemma-existence-projective-cover). The proof (source lines 5626-5660) uses the Stone-Cech compactification of the discretely topologized space for existence, the lifting property and the minimality argument for the extremal disconnectedness of the minimal cover, and the closedness of the comparison map together with the isomorphism criterion for uniqueness (proof lines 5626-5659). The minimality argument and the uniqueness comparison are the substance. H3.
